On "Is this right about how students were assigned to the course: The counsellor offered places first to students on free or reduced lunch and to students whose parents hold no degree; remaining places were open to anyone who asked. Uptake was voluntary. The course was recorded in the 'test preparation course' column, where 'completed' means they got it, and students could have changed whether they got it?": Yes, that's right.
On "Is this right about the change: It was a six-week test preparation course, offered to students, from 1 March to 12 April 2026, before the exam?": Yes, that's right.
On "Is this right about what a row stands for: one student's results from the May 2026 exam at one school?": Yes, that's right.
On "Is this right about 'gender': It was recorded at enrolment, before the exam?": Yes, that's right.
On "Is this right about 'race/ethnicity': It was the school's own grouping, letters A to E, with the mapping not published, and recorded at enrolment?": Yes, that's right.
On "Is this right about 'parental level of education': It was the highest qualification held by either parent, declared at enrolment, with six levels from some high school to master's degree?": Yes, that's right.
On "Is this right about 'lunch': It was standard or free/reduced, assigned by the district when household income is below the federal threshold, making it the low-income indicator, and set before the exam?": Yes, that's right.
On "Is this right about 'test preparation course': It means whether the student completed the prep course, and it was fixed before the exam, but could have been affected by the treatment?": Yes, that's right.
On "Is this right about 'math score': It was the exam mark, 0 to 100, recorded after the exam?": Yes, that's right.
On "Is this right about 'reading score': It was the exam mark, 0 to 100, recorded after the exam?": Yes, that's right.
On "Is this right about 'writing score': It was the writing score, recorded after the exam?": Yes, that's right.
On "Is this right about how rows were sampled: They were sampled by group, including every enrolled student who sat the exam, but not absentees?": Yes, that's right.

On "First, is there anything not in the file that affected both who got the course and how their exam scores turned out?": yes.
On "Next, is there anything in the file that pushed students toward taking the course, but couldn't have affected their exam scores in any other way?": yes.
On "Could a student who took the course have affected the exam scores of a student who didn't?": no.
On "Finally, apart from the course itself, is there any reason why students who took the course would have had different exam scores after the course than those who didn't?": no.
